tour.title: The Agent Orchestrator
tour.description: REEAgent in ree_core/agent.py is the central class that wires the entire RL substrate together — E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal memory, PFC, PAG/amygdala, sleep, affect, and policy all pass through here. With fan-out of 44 it is far and away the highest-connectivity file in ree_core, so understanding what agent.py imports gives you the shape of the whole substrate. Start here to see the vocabulary (z_world, z_self, z_harm, commitments, ghost goals) that the rest of the tour will unpack.

tour.title: The Substrate Config Registry
tour.description: ree_core/utils/config.py holds REEConfig — a monolithic dataclass-of-dataclasses that is the single source of truth for every flag governing the substrate. Sixteen nested config dataclasses are unified by the from_dims factory, which wires sensory/action dims and keyword overrides into the whole tree. Because agent.py and every subsystem imports from here (fan-in 10), reading this file tells you what is tunable and where behavioral variants live.
tour.languageLesson: Python's @dataclass composes naturally into 'dataclass of dataclasses' registries. A single from_X factory that walks the tree and injects overrides is a common alternative to config files or global singletons — every knob has a typed home, and defaults live next to the code that consumes them.

tour.title: The Latent Stack (L-space)
tour.description: ree_core/latent/stack.py implements SD-005's split latent space: separate z_self and z_world encoders, harm-stream encoders, a reafference predictor, and adversarial split heads, glued together by LatentStack into the shared z_beta/z_theta/z_delta context that everything downstream consumes. z_goal (ree_core/goal.py) sits alongside as the slow-decay persistent-goal attractor in z_world space. Together these files establish the representational substrate that E2 rolls forward and E3 selects over.

tour.title: E2 Forward Models and E3 Selection
tour.description: The predictor pair: E2 (predictors/e2_fast.py) runs self- and world-forward models over latent trajectories with contrastive losses and counterfactual rollouts, producing candidate action sequences. E3 (predictors/e3_selector.py) scores those candidates on harm/benefit/residue/goal, arbitrates via a segregated cortico-basal-ganglia dual system, and applies commitment gating to pick the next action. This is the model-based planning core the agent uses on every step.

tour.title: Hippocampal Memory and Ghost Goals
tour.description: The hippocampal system holds episodic history and proposes trajectories back to E3. hippocampal/module.py is HippocampalModule itself — value-flat CEM trajectory proposals under ARC-007, replay/reverse-replay, per-region V_s tracking, and anchor-set management. hippocampal/ghost_goal_bank.py is MECH-292's ranked view over the anchor pool, scoring anchors on a wanting+goal_match+staleness+recoverability composite so the agent can revisit under-served regions. These feed E2's candidate space in Step 4.

tour.title: The Sleep Cycle
tour.description: One of the tightest clusters in the graph. sleep/__init__.py barrels the whole sleep-aggregation subsystem; sleep/phase_manager.py runs SleepLoopManager, the deterministic K-episode FSM (WAKING -> SWS_ANALOG -> PHASE_SWITCH -> REM_ANALOG -> WRITEBACK) that orchestrates the Phase B-E consumers; sleep/routing_gate.py decides which memories flow to which consolidator. Sleep in REE is not idle time — it is where cross-module Bayesian aggregation and self-model updates actually happen.

tour.title: Cingulate and PFC Control
tour.description: The two cortical control clusters. cingulate/__init__.py exports the SD-032 integration cluster (dACC, AIC, pACC, PCC, salience-coordinator, stuck-state-detector) — the salience-and-conflict monitors. pfc/__init__.py exports the PFC-analog subsystem (escape-affordance linker/bridge, frontopolar, lateral-PFC, OFC, trainable escape learner) — the executive-control and reappraisal side. Together they modulate what E3 considers and when the sleep loop should be forced.

tour.title: Regulators and Policy Substrates
tour.description: regulators/__init__.py flatly exports the regulator-layer substrates — GABAergic decay, invalidation trigger, broadcast override, phasic surprise burst, LPB interoceptive routing, liking bridge, simulation-mode rule gate. policy/__init__.py (fan-out 10) exports the pure-arithmetic policy-layer regulators — NoiseFloor, StructuredCuriosity, TonicVigor, CommitMaintenance, GatedPolicy, PolicyChunking/Decomposition, and more. These are the small, composable modules that shape action selection on top of E3's choice.
tour.languageLesson: A __init__.py barrel that re-exports a family of sibling modules gives callers one flat import surface while keeping each substrate in its own file. This is the standard Python answer to what TypeScript does with 'export * from'; it also makes the layer visible in the import graph as a single hub.

tour.title: Residue, Neuromodulation, and Affect
tour.description: The slow-timescale signals that colour everything above. residue/field.py is the RBF-backed distributed representation of residual salience/care markers consumed by the hippocampal and predictor modules. neuromodulation/serotonin.py is MECH-203/204's tonic-5HT state variable with waking rise / REM quiescence dynamics. affect/harm_suffering_accumulator.py is MECH-219, the hysteretic integrator turning medium-timescale unpleasantness into a slow, controllability-gated suffering load. These are the substrates that make REE distinct from a plain RL agent.

tour.title: Bridge: The Coordinator Plan of Record
tour.description: Everything above lives inside ree_core/. The other half of the repo is a completely separate surface: a Phase-3 HTTP daemon that arbitrates experiment claims, ingests TASK_CLAIMS / TASK_CHIPS records, and materializes shared registries into git. coordinator/PLAN.md is the plan-of-record — read it now to see why the daemon exists, what problem the git-as-IPC layer had, the target end-state architecture, the HTTP API contract, the SQLite schema shape, and the phased/reversible rollout. This document frames the next four steps.

tour.title: The HTTP API Surface
tour.description: coordinator/app.py is a pure-stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer (deliberately Flask-free) exposing bearer-authed endpoints for experiment queue claims, task-claim registry mutations, chip ledger operations, the PHASE-4 workspace-state append spool, the recommendation-log append, dispatcher lease upsert, and chip-episode records. It is the coordination-plane API layer for the hub. Note how thin it is — nearly every endpoint delegates straight into db.py in the next step.

tour.title: SQLite Persistence and the Schema
tour.description: coordinator/db.py is the single most-depended-on file in the codebase (fan-in 26) — the SQLite persistence layer that owns schema migrations, atomic claim/queue arbitration, task-claim + chip-ledger ingest authority with a 3-way merge, the PHASE-4 append spools, and orphan-claim reaping. coordinator/schema.sql is the idempotent WAL-mode schema defining the 13 tables it operates on. Together they are the concurrency-correctness kernel that lets many machines write coordination state without stepping on each other.
tour.languageLesson: Two SQLite idioms worth noting: (1) WAL mode (journal_mode=WAL) lets readers proceed while a writer holds a transaction, which is what makes a single SQLite file viable as a many-reader coordination hub. (2) Composite primary keys like (session_id, claimed_at) on task_claims let the same session hold multiple claims over time without inventing a synthetic ID — the key IS the identity, and duplicate inserts fail loudly instead of silently overwriting.

tour.title: The Sole-Writer Sync Daemon
tour.description: coordinator/sync_daemon.py is the Phase-3 sole-writer daemon: it reads coordinator DB state and materialises it into git (result manifests, experiment_queue snapshot, runner heartbeats/status) with dirty-tree guards and conflict recovery. It relies on two partners: manifest_spool.py, the atomic-rename filesystem spool where the /result endpoint parks raw manifest bytes for later commit, and task_claim_chip_git_writer.py, the hub-only materialiser that renders task_claims + chips + workspace_state_entries + recommendation_log_entries into their git-tracked shapes and commits with phase2b:/phase4: prefixes. This is where DB state becomes reproducible git history.

tour.title: Operating the Coordinator in Production
tour.description: coordinator/OPERATOR_GUIDE.md is the capstone — the operator's-eye view of the three-system architecture (git, coordinator API, sync_daemon writers) that Steps 10-13 built up piece by piece. It covers the Explorer coordination panel, the five-phase cutover procedure, hub telemetry transport, troubleshooting, and daemon/config drift diagnostics. Read this last so the failure modes it warns about (dirty trees, conflict recovery, credential wipes) land against a mental model you already have.
